On returning, the group finds the Adventurers Guildhall apparently burning and a Merchant force waiting with the informant. The raid was bait inside Hal's counter-plan: the stockpiled Lamplighter keys were illusions, but the separate deep-gateway key was real and Hal destroyed it. The informant only feigned betrayal to free the former guild leader, and the hall fire concealed a reinforced defense and rapid repairs. The informant disables the attacking house scion's protection. Hal kills him and the surrounding attackers with Anvil Lightning, then nearly continues his assault until Noth, Vorax, and another companion restore his control. The victory raises the Adventurers Guild from F grade to C grade and gives it access to the Lamplighters' real keys. The former leader rejoins, but Hal stays in command. His party survives, yet remains far from Brightsong while Val, Besal, and the absent mistress's unresolved conflicts continue.

characters.description: A Coast Guard veteran in his late twenties who steps outside in boxer shorts and a pair of borrowed Crocs to retrieve his former girlfriend's runaway show cat, minutes before every building on Earth is collapsed by the alien Borant Corporation. Entering the dungeon underdressed and shoeless, he finds the game's System treats his condition as a running novelty and rewards it with unusual bonuses. Practical, stubborn, and slow to anger, he favors his fists and feet, explosives, and careful planning over flash, and from the first floor he refuses to perform cruelty for the watching audience or abandon weaker survivors, a stance that begins to define his reputation.
characters.name: Carl

aliases: Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk
characters.description: A pedigreed Persian show cat belonging to Carl's former girlfriend. An item from one of her first reward boxes raises her intelligence far beyond a normal animal's, and she soon speaks, casts spells, and, on the strength of her superior stats, insists on formal leadership of their two-member party, the self-styled Royal Court of Princess Donut. Vain, imperious, and devoted to her own comfort and status as a champion show animal, she treats Carl as staff as often as partner, yet the two quickly become inseparable and each repeatedly risks everything for the other.
characters.name: Princess Donut

characters.description: Carl's former girlfriend and Princess Donut's owner, away from home when the surface world was destroyed. She never enters the dungeon, but her absence leaves her prize cat in Carl's care and sets the whole story in motion.
characters.name: Beatrice

characters.description: The gruff non-player manager of a tutorial guild hall near the spot where Carl and Donut enter the first floor. After making Carl prove himself against the local goblins, he takes the pair in, walks them through the dungeon's rules, menus, loot, and dangers, and coaches them on how to build their characters. His advice is blunt and transactional at first, but he steadily becomes their most trusted source of guidance.
characters.name: Mordecai

characters.description: A caregiver from the Meadow Lark elder-care facility who entered the dungeon alongside a large group of elderly residents and fellow staff. Calm and quietly formidable, she leads the effort to keep dozens of vulnerable people alive, and her group's alliance with Carl and Donut carries both parties through a major boss fight on the first floor.
characters.name: Imani

characters.description: The alien host of a popular intergalactic interview program who brings notable crawlers onto her show between fights. Shrewd and theatrical, she takes an early interest in Carl and Donut, and her questions and off-air advice give the pair some of their first real insight into how the game and its audience actually work.
characters.name: Odette

characters.description: An elderly, sharp-tongued survivor traveling with the Meadow Lark group on the second floor. Carl helps her reach a safe room during a monster attack, and she repays the debt with loyalty, humor, and open flirtation. Despite her age she is a genuine fighter, and she becomes one of the pair's lasting allies.
characters.name: Elle McGibbons

characters.description: A public-relations liaison assigned to Carl and Donut by the game's operators once the pair start drawing serious audience attention. Zev manages their show bookings and sponsor contacts and explains how crawler appearances on Syndicate programs work, and despite working for the other side becomes genuinely fond of the team.
characters.name: Zev

characters.description: A prince of the Skull Empire, a porcine galactic monarchy whose citizens follow the crawl as entertainment. Carl and Donut first encounter him as a celebrity presence on a rival dungeon program, where he torments human crawlers for sport. Carl's willingness to defy him on the air plants the seed of a dangerous grudge between the crawlers and the Empire.
characters.name: The Maestro

characters.description: A juvenile pack-hunting dinosaur that Donut claims from a reward room near the end of the second floor and, after a fraught taming period involving several bites to her nose, adopts as her beloved pet and mount. Ferociously loyal to Donut, he rounds out the Royal Court as its animal muscle.
characters.name: Mongo

recaps.ending: The book ends with Carl and Princess Donut completing the second floor and descending the stairs to the third. Behind them, the second floor's great crisis is resolved: Carl destroyed the rampaging Rage Elemental with a vehicle rigged full of bombs and an exploit the whole universe watched, after the creature killed Yolanda and other members of the Meadow Lark group. The surviving Meadow Lark residents, shepherded by Imani and the Andrews brothers, went down ahead of them. On the way to the stairs Carl gambled his celebrity on a rival show to help the trapped crawlers Li Jun, Li Na, and Zhang escape, earning the enmity of the Maestro, a prince of the porcine Skull Empire, and Carl's on-air insolence toward the Empire is already infamous. Donut has tamed Mongo, a young dinosaur who joins the party as her pet. In an epilogue on Odette's talk show, the pair discuss the coming race and class selection that will reshape every crawler on the third floor, and Odette leaves Donut with a private piece of advice about choosing a class. The crawler population has fallen below a million, the game's operators are both profiting from and unsettled by the pair's popularity, and Carl goes down the stairs resolved not just to survive the dungeon but to beat the people who built it.
recaps.in_short: The alien Borant Corporation collapses every building on Earth, kills most of humanity, and turns the planet into an eighteen-floor dungeon broadcast across the galaxy as entertainment. Carl, caught outside in his boxer shorts chasing his ex-girlfriend's show cat, enters the dungeon with the cat, Princess Donut, who gains human intelligence from an early reward and becomes a talking spellcaster who insists on leading their party. Guided by Mordecai, a gruff tutorial-guild manager, they fight through the first floor's goblins and bosses, ally with the elderly survivors of the Meadow Lark care facility, and become breakout stars of the broadcast. On the second floor Carl kills a devastating Rage Elemental with a bomb-rigged vehicle in front of the whole universe, the pair appear on Odette's intergalactic talk show, Carl makes an enemy of the Skull Empire's Prince Maestro while rescuing trapped crawlers on a rival program, and Donut tames a pet dinosaur, Mongo. The book closes with the trio descending to the third floor, where every surviving crawler must choose a new race and class.

recaps.text: The alien Borant Corporation instantly collapses every building on Earth, killing everyone inside, and announces that survivors may reclaim their planet by conquering an eighteen-floor World Dungeon whose entrances stay open only briefly. Carl, outside in boxer shorts and his ex-girlfriend's Crocs to retrieve her show cat Princess Donut, has no other way to survive the cold and enters the dungeon with the cat. On the first floor he kills a goblin to earn shelter in a tutorial guild run by Mordecai, who becomes their guide, and completes the tutorial, learning that roughly thirteen million humans have entered and that the crawl is a galactic broadcast run for an audience. A reward from an early loot box transforms Donut: she gains human-level intelligence and speech, and with stats higher than Carl's she formally becomes party leader of the self-declared Royal Court of Princess Donut. Carl, still without shoes or pants, starts to accumulate the fighting skills, oddball achievements, and explosive habits that will define him.

Carl and Donut settle into the rhythm of the first floor: grinding low-level monsters, sheltering in safe rooms staffed by non-player attendants, and learning the dungeon's economy of loot boxes, achievements, and fan attention. They defeat their first boss, an encounter that leaves Carl shaken by how the game dresses its victims. The first broadcast recap episode airs, showing the pair glimpses of other notable crawlers, including the unsettling child prodigy Lucia Mar. They find evidence of crawlers murdering crawlers, tied to a man named Frank Q. Donut discovers the chat system, and her charisma, together with Carl's goblin-friendly tattoo, lets the pair strike a bargain with two goblin engineers, trading salvage for a ramshackle vehicle instead of fighting.

The goblin alliance ends in fire: Carl loots the goblin workshop and destroys it, an act the System memorializes with achievements he is not proud of. The pair earn passes to the Desperado Club, an underground establishment for crawlers, and survive their first direct brush with the player-killers Frank Q and Maggie My, escaping an attempted ambush in a safe room. Riding their goblin-built vehicle east for hours, they follow spray-painted signs left by other survivors and find the people who made them: a band from the Meadow Lark elder-care facility, led by the caregiver Imani with the Andrews brothers and dozens of elderly residents in tow. The two groups exchange stories and begin planning to reach the floor's exit together.

Allied with the Meadow Lark group, Carl and Donut grind the surrounding tunnels, conceal the group's trail, and take down the Juicer, a boss guarding the neighborhood. After a stop at a training guild to learn new spells and finally armor Carl's hands, the combined force fights the area's true gatekeeper, a massive boss called the Ball of Swine, and defeats it using a fortified redoubt. Now level ten, Carl and Donut agree to keep helping Meadow Lark's residents reach safety. As the pair descend toward the second floor they are teleported out of the dungeon to a production trailer: their growing fame has earned them a booking on Dungeon Crawler After Hours, the intergalactic talk show hosted by Odette.

On Odette's show Donut charms the galaxy while Carl studies how the game is packaged for its audience; afterward Odette talks candidly with them about the crawl, the coming race selection, and the fact that random loot is not truly random. On the second floor the pair fight new monsters, and Carl helps the elderly Elle McGibbons to safety as the broadcast warns that Rage Elementals will be released on the floor. Carl weaponizes his growing crafting skill, building his first signature bombs. When the pair try to skip a boss chamber, the boss, a clone of a monster called the Krakaren, comes to them: Carl kills it with a massive explosion and nearly dies shielding Donut with his own body, and Donut, dragging him to safety, admits how much he means to her.

Recovering, the pair find Mordecai transformed into a new body, meet their first Borant dungeon administrator, and gain a public-relations liaison, Zev, who manages their growing celebrity. They rejoin the Meadow Lark group for the push to the stairs, but disaster strikes: a resident's harmless accident triggers the release of a Rage Elemental as punishment, and the creature kills Yolanda and another member of the group before the survivors reach shelter. With the game's rules newly changed to stop crawlers from waiting out the floor in safe rooms, Carl builds a bomb-rigged vehicle and, with the entire universe watching, leads the Rage Elemental on a wild chase and destroys it through a chain of bombs, obstacles, and a rules exploit that becomes an instant broadcast legend.

The Meadow Lark survivors descend to the third floor ahead of them while Carl and Donut finish the second. Pulled onto the sadistic rival show Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem, Carl gambles on his own ratings value to help the trapped crawlers Li Jun, Zhang, and Li Jun's sister Li Na escape an impossible fight, defying the Maestro, a prince of the porcine Skull Empire, whose grudge against Carl becomes public news. The broadcast reports the crawler population falling below one million. Clearing the local kobold territory, the pair defeat the boss guarding the stairwell, and in its reward room Donut claims Mongo, a juvenile dinosaur she tames, after several bites, into her devoted pet. With Mongo in tow, Carl and Donut take the stairs down to the third floor, where every crawler must soon choose a new race and class.

characters.description: A boy who keeps the written log for a covert three-person team watching a remote red house. He records the female target's daily routine while two adult men conduct the observation with him.
characters.name: Surveillance boy

characters.description: One of two adult men conducting long-range surveillance of a woman at a remote red house. He works beside another man and a boy who maintains their log.
characters.name: First adult surveillance watcher

characters.description: The other adult member of the three-person observation team watching a remote red house. The purpose of the methodical surveillance is not yet apparent.
characters.name: Second adult surveillance watcher

characters.description: An unidentified female at a remote red house whose daily routine is being recorded by a covert three-person observation team.
characters.name: Red-house surveillance target

characters.description: The maid in the household at the remote red house where an unidentified female is under covert observation.
characters.name: Greer ranch maid

characters.description: A large traveler staying at a Lubbock motel, where four police officers arrive after a bar confrontation. With no identification and little more than cash and a toothbrush, he needs to get beyond their local reach.
characters.name: Jack Reacher

characters.description: The leader of a disciplined three-person killing crew entering Texas for an undisclosed assignment. She coordinates two male partners through intermediaries and uses false identities, separate travel, and careful trace removal.
characters.name: Female contract killer

characters.description: The tall, fair-haired male member of a professional killing crew arriving in Texas. He follows the female leader's tightly controlled travel and concealment procedures.
characters.name: Large male contract killer

characters.description: A small, dark-haired man who serves as the driver in a three-person professional killing crew. He enters Texas under the female leader's plan and works alongside a taller male partner.
characters.name: Small dark contract killer

characters.description: A composed woman driving a white Cadillac who chooses to pick up Reacher outside Lubbock and takes him south toward Pecos.
characters.name: Cadillac driver

characters.description: A married mother who has spent a month deliberately offering rides to rough-looking strangers. She identifies Reacher as the kind of capable, unattached man she has been seeking and says she urgently needs help that lawyers have not supplied.
characters.name: Carmen Greer

characters.description: A businessman driving a white Mercedes to an appointment. He complies when people posing as federal agents stop him and claim that he must attend an urgent meeting.
characters.name: Al Eugene

characters.description: Carmen and Sloop's six-year-old daughter, named Mary Ellen by the Greer family and usually called Ellie.
characters.name: Ellie Greer

characters.description: Carmen's husband and Ellie's father, the elder son of an old and wealthy Echo County family. His mother, younger brother, and other relatives remain based near the family property.
characters.name: Sloop Greer

characters.description: A woman whose personal bond with Reacher defines the kind of loyalty that could move him to violent retaliation. His feelings toward her help him distinguish that obligation from what a stranger is asking of him.
characters.name: Jodie Garber

characters.description: Sloop's younger brother and a guarded presence at the Red House Ranch. He admits Carmen and Reacher to the house but makes Reacher's access to the family depend on gaining approval for ranch work.
characters.name: Bobby Greer

characters.description: The Echo County sheriff who is waiting at the Red House Ranch when Carmen arrives with Reacher. He directs Carmen inside to hear the news and questions Reacher about his identity.
characters.name: Echo County sheriff

characters.description: Bobby's mother and the apparent authority at the Red House Ranch. She considers hiring Reacher and announces that Sloop's lawyer, Al Eugene, has vanished, though she expects Sloop's release to proceed.
characters.name: Rusty Greer

characters.description: A long-serving Greer ranch hand whom Carmen warns Reacher not to trust. He shares the bunkhouse with Billy and immediately assesses whether the new arrival has the horse skills claimed for him.
characters.name: Joshua

characters.description: A Greer ranch hand and bunkhouse resident who works closely with Joshua. He scrutinizes Reacher's supposed ranch experience and is presented by Carmen as loyal to the family rather than to her.
characters.name: Billy

characters.description: The Pecos district attorney, Sloop's oldest friend, and a candidate for judge. He arrives at the Red House Ranch while the Greers await Sloop's accelerated release.
characters.name: Hack Walker

characters.description: A young Harvard-trained legal-aid lawyer in Pecos who serves clients with little money. Reacher finds her trying to collect an unpaid judgment for a farmworker family, and she agrees in principle to examine Carmen's difficult defense.
characters.name: Alice Amanda Aaron

characters.description: A man who has not paid a $20,000 civil judgment owed to an injured farmworker family. Alice believes he is delaying until the family is forced to leave the area.
characters.name: Lyndon J. Brewer

characters.description: A farmworker family represented by Alice after winning a $20,000 judgment that Brewer refused to pay. Receiving the money allows them to restore basic services, address debts, repair equipment, and continue farming.
characters.name: Garcia family

characters.description: The Garcia family's elder son, killed twelve years earlier while the family was migrating. His parents believe Border Patrol officers were responsible, and the investigation brought no prosecution.
characters.name: Raul Garcia

characters.description: A respected forensic-medicine expert known for defense work. Walker retains him to assess whether Carmen's medical records can support the claim that she suffered abuse.
characters.name: Cowan Black

recaps.ending: Reacher exposes Hack Walker as the organizer of the current killings and the remaining participant in older murders of migrants committed with Sloop Greer and Al Eugene. Walker admits hiring a local surveillance group, having the professional crew eliminate it, arranging Eugene's death, staging Sloop's shooting, and using Ellie's abduction to force Carmen's confession. Rusty shoots Walker after learning the truth, and her remaining shots start the fire that destroys the Red House. Bobby, Rusty, and the maid escape. Reacher and Alice locate the kidnappers' motel near Fort Stockton. Reacher saves Ellie, keeps the surviving crew member alive, and forces a confession that supports Carmen's release. Carmen reunites with Ellie and intends to move to Pecos, settle Sloop's affairs, and consider work or law school. Alice continues handling the legal aftermath. Rusty faces arrest for Walker's death, with leniency expected, while Bobby survives. Authorities connect the conspiracy to more than fifty deaths across seven states. Reacher leaves Carmen, Ellie, and Alice together and resumes hitchhiking west. His relationship with Jodie Garber remains unchanged and unresolved.
recaps.in_short: After escaping trouble with Lubbock police, Jack Reacher accepts a ride from Carmen Greer, who fears her abusive husband Sloop's return from prison and wants him killed. Reacher refuses murder but stays to protect Carmen and her daughter Ellie. Sloop is shot after returning, and a case built from Carmen's confession, medical records, and trust funds appears to prove her guilt. Reacher instead uncovers a frame-up. District attorney Hack Walker, Sloop, and Al Eugene murdered migrants together years earlier. Walker hired professionals to kill Eugene and Sloop, manipulated the evidence against Carmen, and abducted Ellie to compel a confession. Reacher kills two members of the team in an ambush. Rusty Greer kills Walker, accidentally setting the Red House ablaze. Reacher and Alice Amanda Aaron find Ellie, capture her remaining guard, and secure evidence that frees Carmen. Carmen and Ellie plan a new life in Pecos, while Reacher hitchhikes west.

recaps.text: Previously: Jack Reacher left the Army after a career as a military police investigator and continued traveling without a fixed home. Jodie Garber remains his closest personal bond and the standard by which he measures obligations that might justify violence. Their relationship is unresolved as this book begins.

Three unidentified people are methodically watching a remote red house and recording the routine of a school-age girl. Elsewhere, Reacher leaves a Lubbock motel before local police can arrest him over a bar fight with an off-duty officer. A separate three-person contract crew, led by a woman, enters Texas under false identities and prepares a convincing imitation federal vehicle. Reacher escapes south by accepting a ride from an affluent-looking but tense woman in a white Cadillac. She questions him about his rootless life, former Army service, police experience, and willingness to kill. After stopping away from the road, she identifies herself as Carmen Greer. Carmen admits that she has spent a month deliberately picking up rough-looking hitchhikers while searching for a particular kind of man. She says lawyers have failed her, her situation is urgent, and she believes Reacher may be able to help, but she has not yet explained what she wants him to do.

Carmen tells Reacher that she is trapped in the isolated Greer household with her young daughter Ellie. Her husband, Sloop, is serving a federal sentence for tax evasion and may be released within days. Carmen describes years of hidden domestic violence, a hostile family, no independent money, and legal barriers to leaving Texas with Ellie. She admits overstating how recently the assaults occurred, but Reacher accepts that the past abuse was real after testing her account. He also confirms that her poverty is genuine. Carmen says she secretly reported Sloop's tax crimes and expects worse violence if he returns. Reacher offers practical escape plans and agrees to help her and Ellie, but Carmen refuses a life as a fugitive. Her earlier questions about justified killing finally become clear: she selected Reacher because he is an unattached former military investigator who has killed before, and she asks him to murder Sloop. Reacher rejects the proposal. Meanwhile, the professional crew impersonates federal agents to isolate businessman Al Eugene, kills him, conceals his body, and reports success through intermediaries.

Reacher refuses to kill Sloop but agrees to stay for several days and help Carmen and Ellie in some other way. Carmen brings him into Echo County under the false claim that he is an experienced ranch worker. He meets Ellie, gains her initial trust, and travels with mother and daughter to the Red House Ranch. A sheriff's cruiser is waiting there, but the news concerns Al Eugene, Sloop's lawyer, whose abandoned car has been found while he remains missing. Bobby Greer, Sloop's hostile younger brother, controls access to the household. Rusty Greer, the family authority, agrees to consider Reacher for work and confirms that Eugene's disappearance will not delay Sloop's release. Carmen says Rusty despises both her and Ellie and that the family uses Ellie to keep Carmen compliant. Reacher is placed in the bunkhouse with Joshua and Billy, two loyal ranch hands who immediately question whether he knows horses. At the same time, the earlier surveillance team records Carmen bringing Reacher onto the property and recognizes that his ranch-worker cover may be false.

Ellie secretly teaches Reacher enough about saddling a horse to preserve his cover. His growing closeness to Carmen and Ellie provokes Bobby, who warns that the Greers deal personally with outsiders. Carmen continues pressing for Sloop's death and asks Reacher to teach her to use a gun instead, while Reacher keeps urging escape and legal custody proceedings. Bobby claims Carmen has repeatedly brought men into her life. Carmen admits an earlier affair with an unemployed teacher but says Bobby exploited the secret and that ranch enforcers drove the man away. The outside surveillance team is summoned to Coyanosa Draw for new instructions and payment. There, the female-led professional crew ambushes and kills both adult watchers and the boy who kept their log. The crew conceals the scene and leaves. Back at the ranch, Carmen tells Reacher that Sloop suspects she informed the tax authorities and is expected home shortly after lunch on Monday. The deadline is now immediate, and neither the purpose of the surveillance nor the reason for its violent termination is known.

While riding away from the ranch, Reacher finds signs that a three-person team repeatedly watched the Greer property from Coyanosa Draw. Carmen assumes Sloop ordered the surveillance. She produces a legally purchased Lorcin L22 and insists on learning to fire it. Practice shows that she is highly inaccurate even at short range, and Reacher warns that the weapon is suitable only as a last resort. She keeps it. Bobby then sends Joshua and Billy away with Reacher on a supposed feed errand. They take him instead to a remote bar, where the sheriff leaves before the confrontation. Joshua and Billy admit that they mutilated Carmen's former teacher lover and threaten Reacher with the same treatment. Reacher gives them a chance to stop, then attacks first and incapacitates both men before their local allies can intervene. He has defeated Bobby's attempt to remove him, but Sloop's release remains close and Carmen still refuses to flee with Ellie.

Reacher returns to the ranch in Joshua's pickup and forces Bobby into temporary submission. Hack Walker, the Pecos district attorney, arrives as a Greer family friend and helps arrange Sloop's unusually early Sunday release. Another unidentified killing team takes positions near the ranch. Carmen hides the Lorcin L22 in the master suite, rejects Reacher's renewed offer of escape, and plans to confront Sloop. After Sloop returns with Rusty and Hack, Reacher directly warns him that Carmen's treatment is no longer secret. Carmen later reports that Sloop struck her and that he has called law enforcement to remove Reacher. Two Texas Rangers take Reacher toward Pecos because the ranch has ended his employment. Reacher tells Carmen how to contact them directly if violence resumes. The Rangers soon receive a report of a domestic disturbance and race back. They find Sloop shot dead and arrest Carmen. Reacher insists that the case be treated as a claim of self-defense, but Carmen is separated from Ellie and taken toward jail.

Carmen is taken to the Pecos County jail because Pecos handles Echo County court matters. Ellie watches her mother leave in handcuffs, while Rusty and Bobby remain at the ranch. Hack's friendship with Sloop creates a conflict, though officials expect him to recuse himself. Carmen has no lawyer, may face a long delay before bail, and is placed on suicide watch. Reacher stays in Pecos to obtain counsel. He finds Alice Amanda Aaron, a Harvard-trained legal-aid lawyer, while she is trying to enforce a $20,000 judgment for a farmworker family against Lyndon J. Brewer. Alice agrees in principle to represent Carmen but warns that secret domestic abuse will be difficult to prove and that preparing a rapid bail application would require money, records, and expert help. Reacher offers a bargain: if Alice begins Carmen's defense immediately, he will secure the judgment Brewer refuses to pay. Meanwhile, the female-led killing crew watches the Greer ranch, where Rusty, Bobby, and Ellie remain, and prepares for another operation.

Reacher confronts Lyndon J. Brewer at Big Hat Ranch, cuts off telephone contact, destroys valuable property, and threatens further consequences until Brewer writes the overdue $20,000 check. Reacher gives the money to Alice, then meets Hack Walker. Hack presents himself as a reform-minded judicial candidate who will recuse from Carmen's prosecution. He also says the apparent evidence points to planning: Carmen bought the gun after learning of Sloop's release, recruited Reacher, and lied about much of her background. He denies that Sloop abused her and asks whether Reacher might conceal damaging testimony if medical evidence permits a defensible dismissal. Alice advises Reacher to stay off the record because his fingerprints and firearms instruction could strengthen the case. She subpoenas Carmen's medical records. Carmen then repeatedly refuses Alice's representation without explanation. Alice nevertheless delivers Brewer's payment to the Garcia family, whose elder son Raul was killed during an earlier series of attacks attributed to Border Patrol officers. The old investigation produced no indictments.

Ballistics confirm that Sloop was killed with Carmen's Lorcin L22, while Reacher's police-car alibi excludes him as the shooter. Carmen's hospital records document injuries attributed to riding accidents but omit several serious injuries she had described. Defense-oriented forensic expert Cowan Black concludes that the available patterns do not support assault. A jeweler then identifies Carmen's supposedly worthless diamond as valuable, adding another apparent deception. Rusty says family services has removed Ellie. Hack produces records showing Carmen controlled trusts worth nearly $2 million that would become hers if Sloop died, along with her waiver of counsel and a recorded confession. Carmen claims she invented the abuse, pursued Sloop's money, tried to arrange his death in prison, recruited Reacher, and finally shot Sloop herself. Hack chooses a life sentence rather than seeking execution. The combined confession, financial motive, medical opinion, and physical evidence appear conclusive. Believing he badly misjudged Carmen and can no longer help, Reacher prepares to leave Pecos by bus.

Before leaving, Reacher inspects Sloop's body. The two precise forehead wounds were fired from enough distance that Carmen's demonstrated inability with the Lorcin L22 makes her confession implausible. Reacher shifts to Al Eugene's disappearance and predicts where a professional team would have hidden his body. Police find Eugene shot in a limestone crevasse at the location Reacher identifies. The financial records show Carmen made no payment that could explain two professional killings. Reacher then examines her jail contacts and discovers repeated calls from a man falsely claiming to be her lawyer. He concludes that the caller threatened her into confessing. The people who removed Ellie used forged family-services documents, and the agency confirms it never took custody of her. Ellie has been kidnapped to control Carmen. Hack mobilizes police and federal resources, then deputizes Reacher and Alice to obtain descriptions from Rusty. The kidnappers learn that Eugene's body has been found and decide to attack Reacher and Alice while continuing to hold Ellie.

Rusty describes Ellie's supposed social workers as a tall fair-haired man and a fair-haired woman using a large sedan. Reacher recognizes a professional team with a separate driver and concludes that it also killed Eugene. He reasons that Ellie may be kept alive only until Carmen enters a plea she cannot easily withdraw. Rather than search motels and risk her life, he plans to draw the attackers toward himself and Alice. Reacher obtains a sealed file on murders of migrants twelve years earlier. The file records at least seventeen proven deaths, including Raul Garcia, and estimates more victims in an area that includes Echo County. The inquiry ended without identifying the killers. Reacher also resolves the diamond problem: Carmen likely believed the stone was fake because a local jeweler had defrauded her, just as vulnerable migrants were routinely exploited. Her statement was mistaken, not dishonest. With the old killings, the current professional team, and the false case against Carmen beginning to align, Reacher races back to the Red House ahead of attackers traveling in a police-style Crown Victoria.

Reacher commandeers rifles from the Red House and chooses an isolated limestone mesa for an ambush. Alice serves as a witness while he arranges several rifles at separate positions to create the impression of multiple defenders. Three attackers arrive in a pickup. Two figures in false FBI clothing open fire on Alice's empty car, confirming their connection to the impersonations used against Eugene and Rusty. Reacher kills the large male attacker, but the driver escapes while the female leader hunts him through a severe storm. After an exchange of fire in near-zero visibility, Reacher discovers that an earlier shot already killed her. He and Alice identify both dead attackers as members of the trio they had previously seen at a diner. The small dark-haired third member remains elsewhere with Ellie, where he begins preparing a silenced pistol. Reacher and Alice survive the ambush, but they have not captured anyone who can reveal Ellie's location, and the pickup driver is still free.

The escaped pickup returns to the Red House, revealing that its driver used Bobby's vehicle. Hack Walker arrives soon afterward. Reacher confronts him with the improbably polished evidence against Carmen: the inaccessible trust money, the medical packet with missing records, the courier shipment whose weight does not match its contents, and the false federal response. He concludes that Hack reversed Carmen's truthful disclosures into a manufactured murder case. Hack finally admits that he, Sloop, and Al Eugene killed migrant people in the desert twelve years earlier. To protect that secret and his judicial ambitions, Hack first used local watchers around the ranch, then hired the professional crew to eliminate the watchers, murder Eugene and Sloop, frame Carmen, and abduct Ellie. He also posed as Carmen's lawyer and dictated her confession through threats to her daughter. Hack drove the pickup during the mesa attack but fled when the shooting began. He knows the kidnappers use motels and a rerouted telephone number, but says he does not know where Ellie is held. Reacher disarms him as Rusty raises her revolver.

Rusty shoots Hack dead after hearing his confession. Her remaining shots break a lantern and set the Red House on fire. Reacher gets Rusty and Bobby out, then leaves with Alice to find Ellie. They infer that the kidnappers chose a respectable tourist motel near Route 285 and Fort Stockton. The surviving crew member, now alone with Ellie, considers taking her away and then decides to kill her. Ellie tries to escape and hides while Reacher narrows the search by motel layout, occupancy, and vehicle records. He reaches the correct room as the captor drags Ellie toward a silenced handgun, breaks through the window, disarms him, and keeps him alive. The man's confession gives Alice the evidence needed to pursue Carmen's immediate release. State police take him into custody. Carmen is freed and reunited with Ellie the next morning. Authorities connect the case to more than fifty deaths in seven states. Rusty will be arrested for killing Hack but is expected to receive leniency; Bobby survives the fire. Carmen plans to move to Pecos and build a new life with Ellie, while Alice handles the legal transition. Reacher says goodbye and resumes hitchhiking west.
